- When sentiment is high (≥0.7), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.4), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap forecast at 80–82 for 2–3 periods.
- Model consistently underestimates early in 30-day horizon; add 0.5–1.5% to first 3 forecast points.
- If sentiment drops sharply after a peak, model fails to anticipate reversal; adjust downward by 2–4% in next 2–3 periods.
- Model shows persistent lag in capturing sentiment shifts; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 periods when sentiment changes direction.
